subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Henry Ford's Vision
description: A micro-lesson that makes Henry Ford's Vision usable.

hook.text: In 1900, cars were luxury toys for the rich. Henry Ford wanted to change that completely.

buildup.text: Ford grew up on a farm and hated the backbreaking work. He believed machines could free people.

discovery.text: His mission was simple: build a car so cheap that every worker in his factory could own one.

twist.text: Other carmakers mocked him. Luxury cars had fat margins—why build cheap ones?

climax.text: Ford proved them wrong. By 1927, he had sold 15 million Model Ts—more than all rivals combined.

punchline.text: Ford didn't just make cars. He made them for everyone.

quiz.question: How many Model Ts did Ford sell by 1927?

details.summary: Henry Ford envisioned making automobiles affordable for ordinary workers, not just the wealthy, and his relentless focus on efficiency and simplicity transformed the car from luxury to necessity.
details.whyItMatters: Ford's philosophy of mass production and fair wages democratized mobility, created the middle class as we know it, and established manufacturing principles still used today.
takeaways: Ford wanted every worker to afford the car they built
Simplicity and standardization were core to his approach
His vision turned the car from toy for the rich to everyday tool

faq.question: Was Henry Ford the first to make a car?
faq.answer: No. Benz and Daimler preceded him by over a decade. Ford's innovation was not the car itself but the system of mass production that made cars cheap enough for average workers to buy.

faq.question: What made Ford's business approach different from competitors?
faq.answer: While competitors sold expensive custom-built cars, Ford focused on one standardized model produced in massive volume. This drove down costs dramatically through economies of scale.
